title: Scaling Runbook Builder & Compact Pool Controls — prototype + review
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Goal: Design a compact, reviewable "runbook"-style builder for GPU pool autoscaling and burst controls that operators can use to author deterministic scaling policies, preview expected capacity changes, and attach fallbacks. The artifact should exist as a responsive console surface (desktop-first) and a condensed mobile preview for on-call use.

Scope: compact controls UI for per-pool settings (min/max replicas, target latency percentiles, scale step sizes, cooldowns, burst windows), a guided runbook builder with condition blocks (cpu_util, queue_depth, p99 latency, direct traffic spikes), preview simulation of scaling actions, and an approvals/rollout card to attach canary policies. Also includes telemetry hooks and a lightweight cost-estimate strip for each policy.

Prototypes & artifacts:
- Figma prototype: https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/Dedicated-Pool-Runbook-Builder (Frame: "Runbook Builder v2")
- Clickable demo (Figma prototype link): https://www.figma.com/proto/abc123/runbook-builder-v2
- Confluence spec: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/61321/Runbook+Builder+Design+Spec
- Accessibility checklist doc: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/runbook-a11y.md
- Reference telemetry dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/pu_pool_health/pool-ops-overview
- GitHub PR for styles & tokens: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1428

Design decisions & trade-offs:
1) Compact vs full rule editor: chose a block-based compact editor with an "advanced" toggle that expands a JSON rule editor. Rationale: reduces cognitive load for most ops teams while keeping power-user escape hatch.
2) Simulation accuracy: simulation shows expected replica curve for median historical 7d load + synthetic spike. We surface a confidence band rather than absolute guarantees to avoid SLA promises.
3) Cost estimation: show delta estimate for bandwidth of scaling for 1h/24h, presented as relative cost change vs baseline; avoided exact $ numbers to prevent mismatch with billing pipeline.
4) Autoscale step granularity: default step sizes (10%/1 GPU) with ability to pin to exact replica counts; trade-off for stability vs responsiveness documented in notes.
5) Accessibility: ensured all interactive blocks are keyboard-navigable and screen-reader labeled; color choices follow AA contrast.

Review feedback (high level):
- PM (Ethan Ramirez): wants a stronger guardrail for simultaneous burst + scheduled scale-ups to avoid oscillation; requested a new interlock toggle.
- ENG (Jae Kim): asked for explicit plumbing hooks (API fields) for rollout/canary attachment; linked design to runtime-1.18 config schema.
- Observability (Priya Nair): asked that each runbook action produce a deterministic trace ID and quick link to the executions table.
- Design lead (Anya Ford): requested microcopy adjustments for cooldown explanation and to add a single-line explainer for confidence bands.

Decisions made after review:
- Add "interlock" toggle to runbook that deduplicates overlapping triggers (design implemented as a checkbox with explanation tooltip).
- Add an "Execution trace" anchor generated per runbook save that surfaces in pool activity logs.
- Move cost estimate into hover strip to reduce permanent UI noise.

Acceptance criteria:
- Prototype demonstrates creating a runbook from template, adding two condition blocks, simulating a 5x traffic spike, and previewing resulting replica timeline.
- Runbook can be attached to an existing pool and the UI shows the projected cost delta and confidence band.
- Interlock toggle and cooldown microcopy present and validated in a11y pass.
- Engineering has a documented mapping of UI fields to runtime config (linked PR) and a plan for telemetry traces.

Next steps:
- Finalize wording for microcopy (owner: Lena) by 2025-03-05.
- Handoff package to ENG including Figma redlines and JSON schema mapping (owner: Maya).
- UX validation session with two SRE customers (scheduled 2025-03-08).

Notes: Avoid naming this surface "autoscaler" in marketing; prefer "Runbook Builder" or "Scaling Playbook" to emphasize determinism and operator intent.
